q2: SELECT SUM(T) AS SU FROM (SELECT YEAR AS T FROM TEACHES NATURAL JOIN INSTRUCTOR GROUP BY YEAR HAVING COUNT(ID) > 4) AS TEMP GROUP BY T
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT SUM(T) AS SU FROM (SELECT YEAR AS T FROM TEACHES NATURAL JOIN INSTRUCTOR GROUP BY YEAR, COURSE_ID HAVING COUNT(ID) > 4) AS TEMP GROUP BY T
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT SUM(T) AS SU FROM (SELECT YEAR AS T FROM TEACHES NATURAL JOIN INSTRUCTOR GROUP BY YEAR HAVING COUNT(ID) > 4) AS TEMP GROUP BY T
counterexample: INSERT INTO INSTRUCTOR (ID, NAME, DEPT_NAME) VALUES (1, 'Instructor1', 'CS'); INSERT INTO COURSE (COURSE_ID, TITLE, DEPT_NAME, CREDITS) VALUES (101, 'DB', 'CS', 3); INSERT INTO TEACHES (ID, COURSE_ID, SEC_ID, YEAR, SEMESTER, INSTRUCTOR) VALUES (1, 101, 1, 2020, 1, 1), (1, 101, 2, 2020, 1, 1);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because Q1 groups by YEAR, COURSE_ID, and then sums the YEAR, while Q2 groups only by YEAR and then sums the YEAR. This difference in grouping affects the final sum result.
counterexample_dsp: The difference is triggered when there are multiple courses taught in the same year by the same instructor, as Q1 will count each course's YEAR in the sum, while Q2 will only count the YEAR once for that instructor in that year.
